name: memory-dynamics
title: Object 1 Held in Memory
question:
Is the first object's size actually held in the CTRNN's state across the
inter-stimulus interval, when no object is present — i.e. is this real memory?
claim:
Yes. During the ISI (object absent), the agent's neural state encodes object
1's size with correlation 0.88: the trace is set while object 1 falls and
persists through the blank interval until object 2 arrives. Memory realized as
CTRNN dynamics, not a stored value.

expected_behavior.name: obj1-size-held-in-isi-state
expected_behavior.observable: correlation of ISI neural state with s1 over a size sweep
expected_behavior.condition: committed 8-neuron seed, mid-ISI state, s1 swept over [2,6]
expected_behavior.rationale:
The best |correlation| between a neuron's mid-ISI activation and object 1's
size exceeds 0.80 (achieved 0.88 during the real trial). Since no object is present during the ISI,
any such correlation IS a held memory. Verified in tests/test_relational_seed.py.

findings.summary: ISI neural state correlates 0.88 with object 1's size — object 1 is clearly held in persistent memory across the stimulus-free interval.
findings.detail:
figures/memory_dynamics.png shows the mid-ISI activation rising monotonically
with s1 (corr 0.88) and the trace persisting flat through the ISI;
figures/neural_activity.gif shows the memory trace holding across the phase1 |
ISI | phase2 raster.

config.caption: Object 1's size encoded in neural state (corr 0.88) and held across the inter-stimulus interval — the memory trace.
Video — the CTRNN across object 1 | ISI | object 2; the memory trace persists through the blank interval.
The held memory in use — the agent acts on object 2 relative to the remembered object 1.
